source.title: Margaret Kennard (1899-1975): not a 'principle' of brain plasticity but a founding mother of developmental neuropsychology

confidence_rationale: Historical/critical review arguing the 'Kennard Principle' (monotone age-outcome relation) is neither Kennard's nor a principle: developmental-vs-mature outcome is governed jointly by age, lesion staging, laterality, location, number and outcome domain, not by a single law. This SUPPORTS Q-088's core dissociation (mature lesion does not predict the developmental verdict) while WEAKENING any move to generalise one probe into a standing requirement -- which is exactly the scope discipline Q-088 already builds in ('ONE decisive probe, not a standing requirement; do not generalise the protocol before the probe reports'). Its main value is calibrating what a single Q-088 probe can and cannot license.
failure_signatures: There is no monotone law relating developmental to mature disruption; a single decisive probe on one mechanism (e.g. INV-055's infant stage) therefore licenses a conclusion about THAT mechanism only, not about the develop-without protocol as a general standing requirement.

Because outcome is multi-factorial (staging x location x laterality x domain), a Q-088 probe that varies the mechanism but leaves other factors uncontrolled can mis-attribute a dissociation (or an agreement) to developmental necessity when it is driven by a covariate.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The 'Kennard Principle' -- younger-at-injury implies better outcome -- is an oversimplification wrongly attributed to Kennard; her actual work showed outcome after early lesion depends on the interaction of age, staging, laterality, location, number of lesions and outcome domain, and warned against a single-factor rule.
mapping.ree_translation: For Q-088, this is the calibrating caveat. It affirms the premise that developmental and mature disruption dissociate (there IS an age effect), but denies that the dissociation follows a simple predictable law -- so a mature lesion cannot stand in for the develop-without result, which is Q-088's PASS direction. At the same time it warns that the verdict of one probe does not generalise across mechanisms, directly endorsing Q-088's own framing as a single decisive probe rather than a standing requirement.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human developmental-neuropsychology scholarship, not a computational or single-mechanism result; the 'factors' it lists (laterality, lesion number) are brain-specific. What transfers is the epistemic posture -- expect dissociation, do not expect a law, and scope any single probe's conclusion tightly.
mapping.source_context: Historical and critical review of the origins and misuse of the Kennard Principle in developmental neuropsychology; human early-onset brain-lesion literature.

confidence_components.notes: Scholarly, well-cited critical review; included specifically for its bearing on how far a Q-088 probe result can be generalised. Mixed direction: pro-dissociation, anti-over-generalisation.
